note: Technical elements and codes are those of ANSI/ASME/ANS RA-S-1.4-2021, endorsed by NRC Trial RG 1.247. Statuses reflect the current platform implementation.

core.name: Plant operating state analysis
core.blurb: The states the plant can be in — power, shutdown, transition — each carrying its own initiators and success criteria.

core.name: Initiating event analysis
core.blurb: Initiator identification, grouping, and frequency, carried through to the event sequence model.

core.name: Event sequence analysis
core.blurb: Event sequences with linked functional and systemic branches, end states, and transfer logic — including sequences with no consequence, which the licensing case needs.

core.name: Success criteria development
core.blurb: Criteria per sequence and per system, with the supporting calculation recorded alongside.

core.name: Systems analysis
core.blurb: Fault trees, common cause groups, and system notebooks tied to the components they model.

core.name: Human reliability analysis
core.blurb: THERP, IDHEAS, and NUREG-1792 method modules with their inputs kept in the model, not the analyst's head.

core.name: Data analysis
core.blurb: Parameter estimation with distributions and sources attached to every basic event.

core.name: Event sequence quantification
core.blurb: Solving the model as written rather than truncating until it is tractable. PRAXIS is the default solver; SCRAM remains as the reference implementation.

core.name: Mechanistic source term analysis
core.blurb: Release categories derived from the physics of the sequence rather than from a surrogate metric.

core.name: Radiological consequence analysis
core.blurb: Offsite dose and health effects — the metrics RA-S-1.4 actually uses, since core damage frequency and large early release frequency do not apply to many advanced designs.

core.name: Risk integration
core.blurb: Radionuclide sources, operating states, and hazard groups assembled into integrated plant risk, with risk significance applied to the result.

hazards.name: Hazards screening analysis
hazards.blurb: Screening the hazard groups in or out, with the basis recorded.

hazards.name: Seismic PRA
hazards.blurb: Hazard, fragility, and plant response — schemas named SHA, SFR, and SPR after the LWR standard's designators — with a worked HTGR example in the workbook.
